The strongest result is now broader than the special Kerr construction: I have a fixed-time bound on the full spatial resolution of a continually observed, replenished classical field, including coherent hopping and general number-conserving quartic interactions. The key step is a geometric identity that lets thermal diffusion control the fine structure generated by nonlinear flow.

There is also a concrete physical consequence. Two controlled preparations can have identical conditional photon-number populations and identical covariance matrices, yet produce different subsequent records under the same future interaction. A positive current-state predictor resolves that difference, with numerical, preparation-model, and finite-quantum corrections charged separately.

The ordinary-loss argument and benchmark remain unchanged. The results below are additions to the replenishing-system work.

1. A general bound that survives interactions, hopping, and continued observation

Write the field as X∈R2mX\in\mathbb R^{2m}X∈R2m, or equivalently z∈Cmz\in\mathbb C^mz∈Cm, with dynamics

dXt=[FCt(Xt,t)−κ2Xt]dt+κσ2 dBt.dX_t= \left[F_{C_t}(X_t,t)-\frac{\kappa}{2}X_t\right]dt +\sqrt{\frac{\kappa\sigma}{2}}\,dB_t.dXt​=[FCt​​(Xt​,t)−2κ​Xt​]dt+2κσ​​dBt​.

Here CtC_tCt​ is the actual controller state. Its actions may depend on the permitted past record and its retained seed.

The geometric assumptions on each permitted flow are

∇ ⁣⋅FC=0,x⋅FC(x,t)=0.\nabla\!\cdot F_C=0, \qquad x\cdot F_C(x,t)=0.∇⋅FC​=0,x⋅FC​(x,t)=0.

Thus the flow preserves volume and total intensity S=∣x∣2S=|x|^2S=∣x∣2. Number-conserving Hamiltonian flows have these properties.

Define the symmetric part of its Jacobian—the strain of the flow in phase space—by

BC(x,t)=sym⁡DFC(x,t).B_C(x,t)=\operatorname{sym}DF_C(x,t).BC​(x,t)=symDFC​(x,t).

The clean quantitative hypothesis is

∥BC(x,t)∥F≤L∣x∣2\|B_C(x,t)\|_F\le L|x|^2∥BC​(x,t)∥F​≤L∣x∣2

uniformly over the permitted controls. A bounded family of number-conserving quartic Hamiltonians supplies such an LLL. A linear passive hopping term has a skew real Jacobian and contributes zero strain.

The observations are mixed-port counts with intensities

λr(z,Ct)=cr∣ur†z∣2,∑rcrurur†⪯cIm.\lambda_r(z,C_t)=c_r|u_r^\dagger z|^2, \qquad \sum_r c_r u_ru_r^\dagger\preceq cI_m.λr​(z,Ct​)=cr​∣ur†​z∣2,r∑​cr​ur​ur†​⪯cIm​.

The preparation for the simplest statement is

γσ(x)=(πσ)−me−∣x∣2/σ,\gamma_\sigma(x) =(\pi\sigma)^{-m}e^{-|x|^2/\sigma},γσ​(x)=(πσ)−me−∣x∣2/σ,

conditional on the retained initial controller and seed. This conditional preparation requirement matters; an unconditional Gaussian marginal alone would not exclude hidden initial controller correlations.

Let ptp_tpt​ be the current filtering density and define

r(t)=E ⁣[∫pt(x)∣∇log⁡pt(x)γσ(x)∣2dx].r(t)= \mathbb E\!\left[ \int p_t(x) \left|\nabla\log\frac{p_t(x)}{\gamma_\sigma(x)}\right|^2dx \right].r(t)=E[∫pt​(x)​∇logγσ​(x)pt​(x)​​2dx].

The expectation is over the actual record law.

The resulting theorem is

r(t)≤[4cmκ+2L2σm(m+1)κ2](1−e−κt).\boxed{ r(t)\le \left[ \frac{4cm}{\kappa} +\frac{2L^2\sigma m(m+1)}{\kappa^2} \right](1-e^{-\kappa t}). }r(t)≤[κ4cm​+κ22L2σm(m+1)​](1−e−κt).​

This holds at every fixed deterministic time, with a constant independent of the duration of the preceding record. It does not require weak interactions or independent mode intensities. It also does not give a bound on every rare conditional branch or on an adaptively selected stopping time.

The decisive identity

Put

q=log⁡(p/γσ),u=∇q,B=sym⁡DF.q=\log(p/\gamma_\sigma),\qquad u=\nabla q,\qquad B=\operatorname{sym}DF.q=log(p/γσ​),u=∇q,B=symDF.

Direct differentiation gives the flow’s contribution to relative Fisher information:

HF=−2∫p uTBu.H_F=-2\int p\,u^\mathsf TBu.HF​=−2∫puTBu.

A bounded-Jacobian estimate would be poor here because a quartic Hamiltonian has an unbounded, quadratically growing Jacobian.

Instead, integration by parts gives

HF=2∫p B:∇2q+2∫p (∇ ⁣⋅B)⋅u−4σ∫p (Bx)⋅u.H_F= 2\int p\,B:\nabla^2q +2\int p\,(\nabla\!\cdot B)\cdot u -\frac4\sigma\int p\,(Bx)\cdot u.HF​=2∫pB:∇2q+2∫p(∇⋅B)⋅u−σ4​∫p(Bx)⋅u.

The last two terms vanish exactly. Under the two geometric assumptions,

∇ ⁣⋅B=12ΔF\nabla\!\cdot B=\frac12\Delta F∇⋅B=21​ΔF

is itself divergence free and tangent to spheres. The vector field BxBxBx has the same properties. For either such field YYY,

∫p Y⋅∇log⁡(p/γσ)=0.\int p\,Y\cdot\nabla\log(p/\gamma_\sigma)=0.∫pY⋅∇log(p/γσ​)=0.

Therefore

HF=2∫p B:∇2log⁡(p/γσ).\boxed{ H_F=2\int p\,B:\nabla^2\log(p/\gamma_\sigma). }HF​=2∫pB:∇2log(p/γσ​).​

This identity holds for the conditional density; it does not replace that density by equilibrium.

The thermal contribution is

−κr−κσ2 E∫p ∥∇2q∥F2.-\kappa r -\frac{\kappa\sigma}{2}\, \mathbb E\int p\,\|\nabla^2q\|_F^2.−κr−2κσ​E∫p∥∇2q∥F2​.

The observation contribution, after including both normalized no-count evolution and count updates, is exactly

Jobs=E∑r∫p ∣∇λr∣2λr≤4cm.J_{\rm obs} = \mathbb E\sum_r\int p\, \frac{|\nabla\lambda_r|^2}{\lambda_r} \le 4cm.Jobs​=Er∑​∫pλr​∣∇λr​∣2​≤4cm.

The normalization and no-event terms cancel in this calculation; neither has been discarded.

Completing the square yields

r′≤−κr+4cm+2κσ E∥B(Xt,Ct,t)∥F2.r'\le -\kappa r+4cm+ \frac{2}{\kappa\sigma}\, \mathbb E\|B(X_t,C_t,t)\|_F^2.r′≤−κr+4cm+κσ2​E∥B(Xt​,Ct​,t)∥F2​.

Finally, total intensity obeys an autonomous radial diffusion:

dSt=κ(mσ−St) dt+2κσSt dβt.dS_t=\kappa(m\sigma-S_t)\,dt +\sqrt{2\kappa\sigma S_t}\,d\beta_t.dSt​=κ(mσ−St​)dt+2κσSt​​dβt​.

Its stationary law under the specified preparation is Γ(m,σ)\Gamma(m,\sigma)Γ(m,σ), even with adapted tangent feedback. Hence

ESt2=m(m+1)σ2,\mathbb ES_t^2=m(m+1)\sigma^2,ESt2​=m(m+1)σ2,

which closes the bound.

The distinction between total intensity and individual mode intensities is essential. Hopping can destroy the latter’s autonomous dynamics; the proof only needs the former.

The analytic qualification is handled

Ideal count updates can create zeros in a density, where an instantaneous Hessian expression becomes singular. The proof uses positive saturated rates

λε,M=ε+λ1+λ/M,\lambda_{\varepsilon,M} =\varepsilon+\frac{\lambda}{1+\lambda/M},λε,M​=ε+1+λ/Mλ​,

and a radius-preserving cutoff of the nonlinear drift, followed by joint-law convergence and lower semicontinuity of conditional Fisher information.

The cutoff cost is paid. The strain premise itself implies

∣F(x)−DF(0)x∣≤L∣x∣3.|F(x)-DF(0)x|\le L|x|^3.∣F(x)−DF(0)x∣≤L∣x∣3.

The skew linear part is left uncut, and the additional nonlinear cutoff strain vanishes in the radial tail limit. A radial cutoff on the observation rate is avoided because it would introduce an extra, previously uncharged gradient term.

There is also a version for a supplied, correlated initial field/controller law with finite initial conditional Fisher information and finite first two radial moments. It retains those resources explicitly:

r(t)≤e−κtr(0)+4cmκ(1−e−κt)+2L2κσ∫0te−κ(t−s)ESs2 ds.r(t)\le e^{-\kappa t}r(0) +\frac{4cm}{\kappa}(1-e^{-\kappa t}) +\frac{2L^2}{\kappa\sigma} \int_0^t e^{-\kappa(t-s)}\mathbb ES_s^2\,ds.r(t)≤e−κtr(0)+κ4cm​(1−e−κt)+κσ2L2​∫0t​e−κ(t−s)ESs2​ds.

The radial moment in this expression has a closed CIR formula. It is not inferred from the observation record.

The complete proof is in GAUSSIAN_STRAIN_FISHER_THEOREM.txt.

2. What this establishes about effective descriptions

The theorem gives a useful state-selection principle:

Continual replenishment and observation need not force indefinitely increasing spatial resolution of the current conditional field law. The required resolution can be bounded by the observation’s likelihood gradients, the nonlinear flow’s strain, and thermal dissipation.

This removes an obstruction that the earlier draining-budget argument could not address. It also removes the no-hopping restriction from the full-resolution estimate.

Zero strain for linear hopping means that its strength adds no term to this regularity bound. Computing a supplied, time-dependent hopping propagator still has a numerical cost; the theorem does not make that computation free.

Symmetries remove physically irrelevant strain

For two-mode cross-Kerr interaction,

V=gI1I2,Ij=∣zj∣2,V=gI_1I_2, \qquad I_j=|z_j|^2,V=gI1​I2​,Ij​=∣zj​∣2,

the common-phase Hamiltonian g(I1+I2)2/4g(I_1+I_2)^2/4g(I1​+I2​)2/4 acts trivially on the globally phase-invariant conditional laws produced by the stated preparation and passive readouts. Removing it leaves

Vrel=−g4(I1−I2)2.V_{\rm rel}=-\frac g4(I_1-I_2)^2.Vrel​=−4g​(I1​−I2​)2.

Its strain satisfies the exact identity

∥Brel∥F2=g22S2.\|B_{\rm rel}\|_F^2=\frac{g^2}{2}S^2.∥Brel​∥F2​=2g2​S2.

Consequently, with ∣g∣≤g0|g|\le g_0∣g∣≤g0​, the two-mode bound becomes

r(t)≤[8cκ+6g02σκ2](1−e−κt),r(t)\le \left[ \frac{8c}{\kappa} +\frac{6g_0^2\sigma}{\kappa^2} \right](1-e^{-\kappa t}),r(t)≤[κ8c​+κ26g02​σ​](1−e−κt),

including permitted passive hopping. At unit parameters, the uniform constant is 14.

The earlier angular theorem remains productive capital. In its intensity-only regime, angular resolution can be bounded independently of Kerr strength. The broader strain theorem covers more dynamics, while the angular argument can give a better quantitative bound in strong-interaction regimes.

Bounded resolution is not yet an economical closed law

A positive square-root representation makes the consequence precise. If ψ=p\psi=\sqrt pψ=p​, its minimum auxiliary oscillator-number expectation is

Nmin⁡=σ8Iγσ(p).N_{\min}=\frac{\sigma}{8}I_{\gamma_\sigma}(p).Nmin​=8σ​Iγσ​​(p).

A normalized Hermite-amplitude projection through total degree MMM therefore has

E TV⁡(pt,p^t)≤σR8(M+1),\mathbb E\,\operatorname{TV}(p_t,\widehat p_t) \le \sqrt{\frac{\sigma R}{8(M+1)}},ETV(pt​,p​t​)≤8(M+1)σR​​,

where RRR is the appropriate uniform Fisher bound. Squaring the projected amplitude preserves positivity.

But the conservative cost remains severe. For the two-mode R=14R=14R=14 case, a one-percent guarantee gives M=17499M=17499M=17499. Even after crediting exact common-phase symmetry, the sufficient representation contains

223,345,574,375223{,}345{,}574{,}375223,345,574,375

real coefficients.

That is a cost diagnosis of this sufficient bound, not a necessary-memory lower bound. It establishes that a bounded-resolution current description exists in this metric. It does not supply the coefficients, a cheap update rule, or stable repeated compression. Those distinctions remain central.

The exact geometry and coefficient-count checks are preserved in GEOMETRIC_FISHER_IDENTITY_AND_SNAPSHOT_COST_ADDENDUM.txt.

3. A small positive current state for the actual coarse observation

For the constructive case, take two thermally replenished cross-Kerr modes with unit κ,σ,c\kappa,\sigma,cκ,σ,c, initially independent circular Gaussians. Their readout rates are

λ±=12∣z1±z2∣2.\lambda_\pm=\frac12|z_1\pm z_2|^2.λ±​=21​∣z1​±z2​∣2.

Each bin exposes only its first port, or zero if empty. The first trigger time is unreported, and physical evolution continues after that trigger.

For a specified trigger time, the endpoint conditional density has the positive form

f±=(1−w)b2e−bS+wb3e−bS[S2±ηke−δSI1I2cos⁡(φ−vD)],\begin{aligned} f^\pm={}&(1-w)b^2e^{-bS}\\ &+wb^3e^{-bS} \left[ \frac S2 \pm\eta_{\rm k}e^{-\delta S}\sqrt{I_1I_2} \cos(\varphi-vD) \right], \end{aligned}f±=​(1−w)b2e−bS+wb3e−bS[2S​±ηk​e−δSI1​I2​​cos(φ−vD)],​

where

S=I1+I2,D=I1−I2,φ=arg⁡z1−arg⁡z2,S=I_1+I_2,\qquad D=I_1-I_2,\qquad \varphi=\arg z_1-\arg z_2,S=I1​+I2​,D=I1​−I2​,φ=argz1​−argz2​,

and

b>0,0≤w,ηk≤1,δ≥0,v∈R.b>0,\quad 0\le w,\eta_{\rm k}\le1,\quad \delta\ge0,\quad v\in\mathbb R.b>0,0≤w,ηk​≤1,δ≥0,v∈R.

The density is normalized with respect to

dI1 dI2 dθ1 dθ2(2π)2.dI_1\,dI_2\,\frac{d\theta_1\,d\theta_2}{(2\pi)^2}.dI1​dI2​(2π)

6. The remaining construction is now more precise

The broad forward-regularity obstruction has been reduced substantially. Under the stated geometry, bath, kinetic coefficient, and observation assumptions, current conditional density resolution is uniformly controlled even while matter is replenished and observations continue.

The unresolved step is constructive recursive compression. A useful effective law must update a positive numerical state through further marked observations and controls, while keeping both its representation cost and its accumulated prediction error controlled. A bound on the exact filter does not automatically give that property to an implemented approximate filter.

The controller, supplied initial joint law, kinetic coefficients, instrument access, and numerical precision remain part of the scientific problem. New marks can generate additional radial-width mixtures and coherence sectors. The present 400-node construction resolves one actual coarse bin and its subsequent prediction task; it does not establish an economical many-bin closure.

The quantum boundary is equally clear. The two-bin physical bridge is complete for its specified model and readout. The broader strain theorem controls a classical predictive law; it does not automatically replace the backward derivative estimates needed for a general quantum record-error theorem.

The state-selection principle emerging from the completed work is therefore concrete: retain the conditional structure that determines response to permitted interventions, remove transformations invisible to those interventions, and charge the resolution of the remaining structure through the actual observation and dynamical budgets. Populations and covariance can miss that structure. Thermal diffusion can bound its resolution. Turning those two facts into an economical law for long interacting histories remains the consequential next problem.
